overview: Two plant hormones that often work in opposition to control the balance between root and shoot growth.
genZNote: Auxin says 'grow roots.' Cytokinin says 'grow shoots.' Together they negotiate the plant's whole shape.

aspects.label: Main Role
aspects.valueA: Promotes cell elongation, root initiation, and apical dominance.
aspects.valueB: Promotes cell division (cytokinesis) and delays senescence (ageing) of leaves.

aspects.label: Effect on Root/Shoot Balance
aspects.valueA: High auxin-to-cytokinin ratio favours root formation.
aspects.valueB: High cytokinin-to-auxin ratio favours shoot/bud formation.

aspects.label: Effect on Ageing
aspects.valueB: Delays leaf senescence, keeping leaves green longer (the 'Richmond-Lang effect').

overlay.examHighYieldNote: In tissue culture, the auxin:cytokinin ratio is deliberately manipulated to control whether a plant callus grows roots or shoots.
overlay.memoryTrick: Cytokinin drives cytokinesis (cell division). Auxin drives elongation and roots.
overlay.commonMisconception: Cytokinin doesn't act alone to promote shoots — it's the ratio between auxin and cytokinin, not the absolute amount of either, that determines the outcome.
